case_name: Chanchal Rana vs State Of Himachal Pradesh& Others

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Himachal Pradesh & Others, wife's parents-in-law and others

facts_of_case: Informant/wife married to Chanchal Rana in 2020. Wife's family spent more than their capacity to meet demands of husband's family. Husband left for job after 10 days of marriage. Wife's parents-in-law taunted her, demanding dowry and household expenses.

legal_principles.principle: The power of quashing criminal proceedings should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection, and only in the rarest of rare cases.
legal_principles.held: Though there are no limits to the powers of the Court under Section 482 of the Code but the more the power, the more due care and caution is to be exercised in invoking these powers.
cited_cases: Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent patent miscarriage of justice

legal_principles.principle: The Court should apply the test as to whether the uncontroverted allegations prima facie establish the offence or not.
legal_principles.held: If the allegations are so patently absurd and inherently improbable that no prudent person can ever reach such a conclusion and where the basic ingredients of a criminal offence are not satisfied then the Court may interfere.
cited_cases: Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to ensure that the Court does not unduly interfere

legal_principles.principle: The High Court should not unduly interfere, and no meticulous examination of the evidence is needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.
legal_principles.held: No meticulous examination of the evidence is needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.
cited_cases: Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to prevent the High Court from unduly interfering

legal_principles.principle: Where there is an express legal bar enacted in any of the provisions of the Code or any specific law in force to the very initiation or institution and continuance of such criminal proceedings, such a bar is intended to provide specific protection to an accused.

cited_cases: Amit Kapoor v. Ramesh Chander, (2012) 9 SCC 460
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to provide specific protection to an accused
